Subject: Halcyon security questionnaire — follow-ups on residency + deletion

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the initial answers your team sent yesterday. Procurement is reviewing the legal language but security has a couple of follow-ups specifically around: (1) whether hosted API request/response data ever leaves the EU for processing, (2) backup retention and deletion guarantees (we need explicit max timelines), and (3) evidence we can include in our compliance pack (audit log extracts, KMS attestation, deletion runbooks).

Could you confirm:
- Are request payloads routed outside the EU under any normal operating mode? If yes, under what conditions (failover/observability)?
- For tenant data tied to hosted API usage, what is the timeline for active storage, snapshot backups, and final deletion from backups?
- Do you provide an attestation or canned report we can ship to our auditors?

We're trying to scope a procurement schedule and will need concrete timelines for our retention clause. Apologies for the rapid questions — we want to avoid an extra legal loop later.

Best,
Sasha
Security Lead, Halcyon Financial

Hi Sasha — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary up front, full details below and a short evidence pack attached.

Summary answers (short):
1) EU-only processing: By default in our EU-hosted offering, request/response processing and KV/prefix caches are routed to EU regions only and are not routed internationally. We do have documented, policy-driven failover behaviors that restrict cross-region routing to emergency scenarios; these are opt-in by customers.
2) Retention timelines: Transient request data for hosted API endpoints is kept in in-memory caches for up to 2 hours. Operational traces and logs used for debugging are retained for 30 days by default; backups/snapshots are retained for up to 90 days. Final deletion from backups occurs during our scheduled snapshot pruning (maximum 120 days from snapshot creation under default retention).
3) Evidence & attestation: Attached is a one-page attestation and a retention_matrix_hostedapi.xlsx with the retention guarantees, deletion windows, and the steps we take for backup prune + verification. We can also provide a redacted sample of audit logs showing erase operations (subject to NDA).

Full details:
- Routing and processing
  - Primary routing: Customer API endpoints in the EU are terminated at EU ingress gateways and served by EU compute clusters. Model inference executions, KV cache, and temporary artifacts are persisted only to EU block/storage volumes configured for the customer.
  - Failover & emergency routing: Our Smart Routing component has a documented policy for region failover (e.g., if all EU availability zones in the region are degraded). Failover that routes requests outside the EU requires an explicit customer configuration (cross-region-fallback: allowed) and is not enabled by default. For enterprise customers with legal constraints we can disable cross-region failover entirely.
- Active & backup retention
  - Active artifacts: Generated responses and request metadata required for billing/monitoring are stored for up to 30 days in EU storage when billing/observability is enabled.
  - Snapshots/backups: Snapshots are taken daily for redundancy; default snapshot retention is 90 days. Backup pruning runs weekly; a snapshot will be eligible for prune after 90 days and deleted within 30 days of becoming eligible (max 120 days from creation).
  - Hard-delete propagation: When a customer requests tenant-level erasure, we delete active objects immediately and create a deletion token; snapshot pruning then removes residual data during the scheduled prune run. We track deletion operations in an audit ledger and verify checksum differences post-prune.
- Deletion SLA and proof
  - Timeline: erasure request => active delete within 24 hours (business hours), snapshot purge scheduled at next prune window (within 7 days of request) and completed within the subsequent prune cycle (max 30 days after eligibility). Max practical end-to-end from erasure request to no-residual-backup-state: 120 days.
  - Auditability: We can provide an extract from the immutable audit ledger (timestamped event showing deletion request, deletion token issuance, snapshot prune events) and a signed KMS key rotation note to show key material removal for encrypted snapshots.
- Encryption & keys
  - Data at rest: all EU-hosted storage is encrypted with AES-256. Customer data encryption keys are either Redwood-managed KMS keys (default) or customer-managed keys via supported KMS (bring-your-own-key). When BYOK is used and a customer deletes the key, that provides cryptographic infeasibility of access beyond logical deletion.

I'll attach the brief evidence pack. If you need a formal attestation letter on company letterhead we can route to our compliance team (cc'd: Marissa).

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Security, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

Hi Sasha — adding a technical note on backups and deletion verification so your auditors get the specifics they usually ask for.

Technical verification steps we include in our evidence pack:
- Snapshot lineage: each snapshot has immutable metadata (creation timestamp, source cluster ID, and included object hashes). On purge we record a prune event referencing the snapshot IDs removed.
- Deletion tokens: when tenant erasure starts we issue a deletion token tied to affected objects; that token is referenced in prune logs so auditors can map request -> prune event.
- Cryptographic controls: snapshot payloads are encrypted per-tenant. If BYOK is enabled and a tenant revokes/disables the key, we include a signed KMS revocation statement in the evidence bundle.
- Sample artifacts: we can produce (a) a redacted audit ledger extract covering a single tenant erase and (b) a signed statement of the prune run that removed the snapshot. Both are suitable for inclusion in an auditor pack under NDA.

If Halcyon wants a short walkthrough we can set up a 30-min call with our infra team next week — happy to demo the prune verification flow and show the audit tokens.

Best,
Marissa
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
